sections.title: Saying What You Want
sections.content: 'Querer' means to want, and it is the verb you order with. It is stem-changing: the e in the stem becomes ie in every form except nosotros and vosotros. Once you have 'quiero', you can put a noun after it — 'quiero un café' — or a second verb in the infinitive — 'quiero comer'.

sections.title: Two regular verbs: tomar and comer
sections.content: 'Tomar' (to have a drink, to take) and 'comer' (to eat) are regular — an -ar verb and an -er verb — so they take the ordinary endings and the stem never changes.

items.english: Do you want to have a coffee?
I also want to eat something.
What would you like? (a waiter, to more than one person)

sections.content: The stem change is easy to hear: 'quiero' and 'quieres' have the ie, 'queremos' does not. If you can hear it, you can conjugate it.
